title: The Scout's GW6 squad for Wildcarders and new starters
body:
The Scout uses form and fixtures to build a Wildcard squad ahead of the Gameweek 6 deadline in Fantasy Premier League at 11:00 BST on Saturday 10 October.

Managers who are creating a new team for the Second Chance League will also be able to pick these 15 players.

Saka in Arsenal triple-up 

The return to full fitness of Arsenal playmaker Martin Odegaard (£6.8m) has allowed Bukayo Saka (£9.5m) to focus on posing a big goal threat early on this season.

Saka’s six big chances (situations where a player is expected to score) are more than any other midfielder in Fantasy, while his 12 shots in the box are joint-second.

With first-choice penalty-taker Viktor Gyokeres (£7.1m) struggling to get minutes this season, Saka now has spot-kick duties to further his appeal as a big-hitting captaincy option. 

Doubling up at the back still looks a very strong tactic, bearing in mind that three of the four goals Arsenal have conceded this season have come from outside the box.

At a cost of only £4.6m, Ezri Konsa is an obvious value pick as a route into a defence that kept 19 clean sheets last season.

The Gunners’ resilience helped David Raya (£6.1m) win the Golden Glove award in 2025/26 and the Spaniard is by far the goalkeeper most likely to keep a clean sheet in any given Gameweek.

Double-ups on Brighton, Chelsea and Fulham 

Brighton & Hove Albion's 3-0 win over Arsenal means they have now scored at least three goals in four of the first five Gameweeks.

Crucially, the data also backs up their performances - their 63 shots in the box rank joint-top, while their 22 big chances are five more than any other side apart from the 20 of Sunderland. 

Pascal Gross (£5.8m) has soared to the top of the overall player standings, claiming 47 points thanks to three goals and four assists. The German's dominance of dead-ball duties (including penalties) means Fantasy managers should play him regardless of opponent right now.

Brighton centre-back Luka Vuskovic (£5.0m) could be a great differential pick. Owned by only three per cent of managers, he has combined a goal with three clean sheets and four defensive contribution (DC) points. 

While the Seagulls have proven themselves fixture-proof, the double-ups on Chelsea and, in particular, Fulham, are very much driven by their schedules.

According to the Fixture Difficulty Ratings (FDR), with a ranking of one awarded to the easiest fixture and five to the hardest, only one of Chelsea's next eight matches scores more than three, in a run that continues into December.

Cole Palmer's (£9.7m) all-round potential makes him worth the extra outlay over Morgan Rogers (£7.7m) to pair up with their highly-owned forward Joao Pedro (£7.7m), who sits in over 65 per cent of squads.

Penalty-taker Palmer leads Rogers by 12 shots in the box to four and has created four big chances to his rival's two. 

Investment in Fulham pair David Affengruber (£4.5m) and Gonzalo Garcia (£6.0m) is far more short-term, with the Cottagers facing all three promoted clubs in successive matches over Gameweeks 6-8.

Centre-back Affengruber has collected DC points in both of his starts this season, while forward Garcia has had more shots, shots in the box and big chances than any team-mate.

Look for good value in midfield, rather than up front

When assessed by position, the budget midfielders have made a far more persuasive case for inclusion in our squads than their counterparts up front.

Five of the 10 top-scoring midfielders over the first five Gameweeks are priced under £6.5m - along with Gross, Brentford's Kevin Schade (£6.2m) and AFC Bournemouth's Marcus Tavernier (£6.1m) have shone in the cut-price bracket.

Schade has produced three goals and two assists, while his 12 shots in the box are level with Saka and Palmer.

Tavernier has also scored three goals and, despite failing to earn any assists, has created three big chances.

Among forwards, by contrast, three of the four most expensive assets - Erling Haaland (£15.6m), Joao Pedro and Alexander Isak (£9.1m) - are also the top scorers, highlighting the lack of favourably-priced options up front.
